title: POC Multilang Knowledge Extractor Workshop - Sandbridge Labs
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC to validate a multilingual knowledge-extraction pipeline for Sandbridge Labs. Discussed success criteria (precision/recall on entity pairs, latency SLO, cost envelope), workload sizing (peak qps and daily tokens), benchmark plan (human eval + automated metrics), and shortlisted open models with tradeoffs. Agreed on deliverables: SOW, 200-sample test corpus, and initial micro-benchmarks run by Redwood.
next_steps: Jordan to send draft POC SOW and pricing by 2026-07-20
Marco to upload 200 de-identified sample documents + labeling guide by 2026-07-18
Priya to run a micro-benchmark (latency & mem) across 3 shortlisted models and share results by 2026-07-23
Schedule a 45-min bench review meeting week of 2026-07-27
action_items: Jordan Lee: Draft SOW and include dedicated vs hosted cost scenarios (due 2026-07-20)
Priya Natarajan: Run batch and single-request latency tests on 13B and 7B variants; capture CPU/GPU mem and token throughput (due 2026-07-23)
Marco Ruiz: Provide 200 representative docs and a short labeling spec (due 2026-07-18)
Evan Cho: Confirm VPC peering and KMS requirements for POC (due 2026-07-21)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-16
- Start: 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tomas (Redwood Solutions), Marco (Sandbridge), Aisha (Sandbridge Product), Evan (Sandbridge Infra), Nina (Sandbridge DS)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the POC shape for the knowledge extractor that you described in the email. does that agenda look right?
[00:18] Marco: yeah that looks good. we want to make sure the POC proves both quality across languages and that we can meet operational constraints — basically accuracy + SLOs + cost.
[00:34] Priya: great. could you quickly restate the top success criteria so we're aligned?
[00:40] Aisha: sure - primary is extraction accuracy for entity-link pairs across english/spanish/japanese, target is F1 > 0.82 on our internal gold set, and precision for relation extraction > 0.85. secondary is latency — we need median request latency < 350ms for single-request mode and tail (p95) < 1s under our expected load. third is run-cost; we gave a rough budget of ~$4k/month for production, for the POC we'd like a clear estimate so we can evaluate hosted vs dedicated.
[01:10] Jordan: good specifics. Marco, can you confirm expected traffic pattern? peak QPS and daily volume?
[01:19] Marco: baseline is 5 qps, bursty up to ~35 qps during ingest windows. daily token volume around 1.2M tokens, but most ops are short queries ~150-400 tokens.
[01:35] Priya: okay that helps size batching and memory. for benchmarks we'll run single-request and batching scenarios, plus a cold-cache vs hot-cache run to capture KV-cache impact.
[01:48] Nina: on languages — our spanish is mostly latin-american scientific style text, japanese has mixed kana/kanji and domain terms. we also have some portugese coming later but that's lower priority.
[02:02] Tomas: makes sense. for model selection, we'll balance multilingual capability, domain robustness, and cost. priya and i put together a shortlist to discuss.

[02:18] Jordan: let's walk through the candidate models and the tradeoffs. Priya over to you.
[02:22] Priya: sure. shortlist A (smaller, cost-friendly): Mistral 7B-style open variants and Llama 2 7B. These are good for throughput and cheaper inference but may struggle with nuanced domain terms and japanese tokenization out of the box. Shortlist B (mid-size): Llama 2 13B, Mistral 14B. Better language coverage and quality, still feasible on high-memory instances. Shortlist C (quality-first): Falcon 40B / fine-tuned 30-40B mixes; these hit higher quality especially for domain reasoning but cost and latency are higher. also noted some newer polyglot-tuned models in the community that are promising but with less benchmark history.
[03:05] Marco: our priority is multilingual quality first, then cost. if the 13B hits your F1 target with cheap fine-tuning, that would be ideal.
[03:12] Priya: yes that's often the sweet spot. we should run zero-shot and 100-shot-ish prompt templates, then a small fine-tune (PEFT / LoRA) on your 200-sample dataset to see delta.
[03:25] Aisha: on evaluation, we want automated metrics (F1/precision/recall) and then a small human review of edge cases. how do you normally run the human eval?
[03:34] Tomas: we typically sample 100 edge cases post-filtering and have 3 raters. we track inter-annotator agreement and qualitative notes. we'll include a short rubric for you.

[03:50] Jordan: on infra we briefly discussed hosted vs dedicated. Evan, any constraints?
[03:56] Evan: security is primary — we need SOC2-level audit logs, SSO integration, and KMS for key management. for the POC we can do VPC peering to a hosted Redwood Private plane if that's an option, or run in our cloud with Redwood images. we also need to establish data retention policy — POC data should be ephemeral and not stored beyond 30 days.
[04:20] Priya: Redwood supports VPC/private deployments and we can enable KMS. the hosted route is quicker but for your compliance we can propose a Private POC with peered networking. that will change latency slightly but gives isolation.
[04:35] Marco: cost delta? we need to see numbers.
[04:38] Jordan: we'll include cost scenarios in the SOW: hosted (per-token pricing + minor infra) vs dedicated reserved GPUs (monthly commit) vs private (license + infra). for the short POC we often recommend hosted or dedicated ephemeral to avoid infra ops.

[04:55] Priya: benchmark plan — proposed steps:
- seed: run 3 models zero-shot (Llama2-13B, Mistral14B, Falcon-like 40B) on 200-sample corpus, measure F1/precision/recall and latency
- tuning: run LoRA with 200 examples (few-token fine-tune) on 13B and 14B, measure delta
- stress: run burst QPS test to verify p95 latency under 35 qps and batching configs
- human: sample 100 edge cases for manual review

[05:35] Aisha: that timeline — how long for each step?
[05:38] Priya: initial micro-bench (zero-shot) we can do in 3 business days after we have the samples and IAM/VPC access. LoRA runs will take another 4-5 days including hyperparam tuning. the stress tests can be done in parallel but schedule-dependent. overall we estimated 3-4 weeks for the POC to complete all artifacts.
[05:58] Marco: OK good. what about quantization? we want cost savings but not big quality drops.
[06:04] Priya: we can test 4-bit q8/4 QAT-style setups; many 13B models retain most quality at 4-bit with substantial cost reduction. we'll capture eval deltas in the bench report.
[06:18] Jordan: any compliance questions left?
[06:20] Evan: just one — audit logs retention and ability to export.
[06:24] Tomas: Redwood Console exposes per-request logs and you can export to S3; retention configurable based on plan. we'll document exact retention limits in the SOW.

[06:36] Nina: one more data note — docs have lots of tables and formulas; should we include parsing of table content or treat it as context?
[06:45] Priya: this POC will focus on text extraction; table parsing is a complex sub-problem. we can flag table-heavy docs and run a limited parser or fallback to OCR-to-text for first pass. discuss as a stretch goal.

[06:58] Jordan: recap of what we agreed: success metrics (F1 targets, latency), workload sizing (5 baseline, 35 bursts, ~1.2M daily tokens), shortlist for bench (Llama2-13B, Mistral14B, Falcon40B as quality baseline), security constraints (VPC, KMS, audit logs), timeline (~3-4 weeks), deliverables and owners.
[07:20] Marco: yep. also we'll have an internal stakeholders sync once we see the micro-benchmarks.
[07:26] Jordan: perfect. priya and i will get the SOW out, priya will kick off bench runs once we have the sample set and access.
[07:34] Aisha: thanks, looking forward to the SOW.
[07:36] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench review.

End of meeting.
